comment: Overhead electric lines are shown on site plan (Sheet 9) along western boundary and running east-west across northern portion of site. However, no building elevation sheets with surveyed overhead conductor elevations are provided. Without elevation data showing conductor heights and building face/roof elevations, the 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance requirement cannot be verified for any building. Applicant must provide surveyed conductor elevations on building elevation sheets with dimension callouts showing clearances from outside conductor to all building faces, overhangs, and projections.
applicableAreas: Building facades and projections on all 8 buildings

comment: The site plan does not specify the conductor type (primary, neutral, secondary) or voltage classification of the overhead electric facilities. The extensive transmission notes on Sheet 3 suggest these may be transmission facilities (≥60kV), which would have different clearance requirements (UCM § 1.14.0) than distribution facilities (<60kV). Without specification of conductor type and facility classification, the 15-foot radial clearance requirement for distribution facilities cannot be verified as applicable. No clearance dimensions from outside conductor to any customer facility are shown on site plan or detailed sheets.
applicableAreas: All customer facilities (buildings, parking, structures)

comment: All 8 proposed buildings include roof overhangs and eaves as standard townhome construction. No building elevation sections, detail sheets, or cross-sections are provided showing the surveyed position of overhead conductors relative to building projections. Without elevation data and clearance dimension callouts, compliance with 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances for projections cannot be verified. Applicant must provide building elevation or section views showing overhangs, awnings, balconies, decks, and roof edges dimensioned from surveyed overhead conductor positions.
applicableAreas: Buildings with projections (all 8 buildings show eaves/roofs)

comment: Site plan shows concrete and decomposed granite walkways connecting buildings. If these walkways are elevated relative to grade (as typical in multi-family developments), they would be elevated platforms potentially requiring the 15-foot radial clearance. However, no elevation data is provided showing whether walkways are at-grade or elevated, and no vertical clearance dimensions from overhead conductors to walkway height are shown. Applicant should clarify walkway elevations and provide section views with clearance dimensions if walkways are elevated and within potential clearance distance of OHE.
applicableAreas: Elevated walkways or platforms if any exist

comment: Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4) shows overhead utility poles located outside the western property line in the Valley View Road right-of-way, with overhead lines running along the road and extending onto the property. Buildings 1 and 2 are positioned near the western property boundary in proximity to these ROW-adjacent electric facilities. However, no clearance dimensions are shown on site plan indicating the distance from building faces to the outside conductor of the overhead lines in the adjacent ROW. Applicant must provide dimension callouts on site plan and building elevations showing the 7.5-foot horizontal and 15-foot radial clearances are maintained from ROW-located overhead electric facilities to all buildings.
applicableAreas: Buildings adjacent to western ROW (Valley View Road)

comment: No building elevation sheets with surveyed overhead conductor elevations are included in the site plan package. The Preliminary Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) references 'See Sht. 19 for Profile' but that sheet contains water/wastewater utility profiles, not overhead electric conductor elevations. All 8 proposed buildings are positioned in proximity to documented overhead electric facilities (shown on Existing Conditions Survey and Site Plan), yet no surveyed conductor elevation data or clearance dimension callouts appear on any building elevation sheets. Applicant must provide registered surveyor field survey data showing existing overhead conductor elevations and clearance dimensions to all building features, with at least mid-span clearance measurements if vertical clearance appears marginal.
applicableAreas: All buildings and elevated structures

comment: No enlarged plan detail sections or cross-section views are provided showing dimension lines extending from the outer electric conductor to the outermost edge of buildings and building projections. While the site plan shows OHE line routing, no specific clearance dimensions or section views with conductor-to-building edge dimensions are depicted. Applicant must provide enlarged plan details and section views for all buildings within potential clearance distance of overhead facilities, with dimensions clearly labeled from outer conductor to all building faces, eaves, and roof projections.
applicableAreas: All buildings within potential clearance distance of OHE

comment: Site plan shows wooden privacy fences along portions of the property perimeter. Overhead electric lines are shown in proximity to the western boundary (in the Valley View Road ROW) and running east-west across the northern portion of the property. However, no dimension callouts show the clearance from the outside conductor of the overhead electric lines to the fence structures. Applicant must provide dimension annotations on site plan and fence detail sheets showing the 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance is maintained from the outside conductor (not pole center) to all fences.
applicableAreas: Fences along property perimeter

comment: Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4) shows utility poles located both outside the western property line (in Valley View Road ROW) and within the property boundaries. Site plan shows wooden privacy fences along portions of the property perimeter. However, no dimension callouts on the site plan verify that fence posts maintain the 10-foot horizontal clearance from existing electric pole locations. Applicant must provide dimension annotations showing fence post locations maintain minimum 10-foot clearance from all existing utility pole centers.
applicableAreas: Fence posts adjacent to existing electric poles

comment: Sheet 3 contains extensive Electric Transmission Notes indicating transmission facilities are present on or adjacent to the site. The notes reference transmission lines, transmission structures, and transmission easements. However, the site plan does not clearly specify whether proposed fencing is located beneath or within transmission easements. Additionally, no detail sheets are provided showing fence material specifications (conductive vs. non-conductive) or grounding detail drawings. If fencing is proposed within transmission easement areas, applicant must provide fence detail sheets with material specifications and grounding designs as required.
applicableAreas: Proposed fencing beneath or adjacent to transmission lines

comment: Site plan shows retaining walls throughout the site (documented on Wall Plan sheets 38-39 and visible on Site Plan sheet 9). Overhead electric lines are shown on the site plan running along the western boundary (in ROW) and east-west across the northern portion. However, no dimension callouts show the clearance from the outside conductor of the overhead electric lines to retaining wall faces. Applicant must provide dimension annotations on site plan and wall section details showing the 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance is maintained from the outside conductor to all retaining walls in proximity to overhead electric facilities.
applicableAreas: Retaining walls near overhead electric lines

comment: Wall Plan detail sheets (38-39) are provided showing cross-sections of retaining walls throughout the site. However, none of these section views include the overhead electric conductor elevation or dimension callouts showing clearance from the conductor to the outermost edge of wall construction. Applicant must provide revised wall section views showing surveyed overhead conductor elevation and clear dimension lines from outer conductor to wall face for all walls located within potential clearance distance of overhead facilities.
applicableAreas: Retaining walls within clearance distance of OHE

comment: Site plan shows interior driveways and parking areas. Overhead electric lines are documented on existing conditions survey and site plan. However, no grading plan section views or profiles are provided showing finished driveway/parking grade elevations with clearance dimensions to overhead electric facilities. The reference 'See Sht. 19 for Profile' on Sheet 21 is incorrect; Sheet 19 addresses water/wastewater utilities, not overhead electric. Applicant must provide grading plan cross-sections at driveway/parking areas showing finished grades and overhead conductor heights with vertical clearance dimensions. If clearances appear marginal, registered surveyor mid-span clearance data is required to verify compliance with 16-foot (parking without trucks) or 18-foot (truck traffic) minimums.
applicableAreas: Driveways and parking areas on site

comment: Sheet 3 documents extensive transmission facility requirements indicating transmission lines (voltage ≥60kV) are present or will be present on/adjacent to the site. However, no specification of transmission voltage or routing directly over driveways is provided. If transmission lines cross over internal driveways, the site plan must show finished driveway grades with vertical clearance dimensions demonstrating 30-foot minimum clearance from transmission conductor to ground surface. Applicant must clarify transmission line routing and provide grading plan sections with clearance dimensions if transmission lines cross driveway areas.
applicableAreas: Driveways and roads if transmission lines exist above

comment: Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4) shows a utility pole located within the property boundaries in the northern portion of the site, within the depicted electric easement area. Site plan shows internal driveway routing through the site. However, no dimension callouts or notes indicate whether this existing pole will be relocated or maintained, nor is the driveway alignment shown at sufficient detail to determine if there is a conflict requiring 30-foot minimum pole relocation. Applicant must clarify the status of existing on-site utility pole(s) and verify that any driveway alignments maintain minimum 30-foot distances from poles or confirm that poles will be relocated to resolve conflicts.
applicableAreas: Areas where driveways intersect electric poles

comment: While overhead electric lines are shown on the site plan, grading plan, and landscape plan as linear routing, NO clearance dimensions are shown anywhere in the plan set—neither from outside conductor nor from pole centerline. This makes it impossible to determine whether any clearance dimensions that do exist are measured correctly from the outside conductor (as required) or incorrectly from pole center. However, the fundamental issue is that clearance dimensions are entirely absent, making this specific verification unnecessary because there are no dimensions to evaluate for correctness. The absence of any clearance dimensions throughout the plan set is the primary deficiency (covered under other items).
applicableAreas: All overhead electric clearance dimensions

comment: Site plan shows 'Construct 5' Concrete Sidewalk' along the western property frontage on Valley View Road. Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4) shows existing utility poles located in the ROW along Valley View Road near the property corners. However, the site plan does not include dimension callouts showing that the proposed sidewalk maintains clearance from existing power poles at each end of the property along the ROW frontage. Applicant must provide dimension annotations or notes confirming that the proposed sidewalk is properly routed to avoid contact with existing power poles at the north and south property line intersections with Valley View Road.
applicableAreas: Sidewalks at western property boundary along Valley View Road

comment: Sheet 3, Electric Transmission Notes #16 explicitly states: 'Owner may not place, erect, construct or maintain the following within electric transmission easement: any permanent structures, including, but not limited to habitable structures such as homes, mobile homes, garages, or offices.' The Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4) shows a utility pole within a 15' Electric Easement in the northern portion of the property. The site plan does not clearly delineate this transmission easement boundary, and does not confirm that no proposed structures, walls, or improvements are located within the documented transmission easement. Additionally, the site plan does not show clearance dimension callouts demonstrating 7.5-foot clearance from outside conductor for any items that may be placed at the easement edge. Applicant must clearly depict the transmission easement boundary on the site plan and verify that no buildings, structures, walls, or other customer facilities are installed within the easement. If any improvements are located within the easement boundary, they must be relocated outside the easement.
applicableAreas: All customer facilities within electric transmission easement

comment: Overhead electric facilities are documented on the site plan as existing infrastructure. Based on the extent of transmission facility notes on Sheet 3 and the pole locations shown on the Existing Conditions Survey, overhead conductors appear to be present on or very near the site. Proposed site features (driveways, parking areas, buildings) are in close proximity to documented overhead electric infrastructure. However, no registered surveyor field survey data is provided showing actual pole locations, conductor elevations, or mid-span clearance measurements. Without surveyed data confirming that vertical clearances meet the 16-foot (parking), 18-foot (roads), or 7.5-foot (horizontal) minimums, mid-span clearance verification cannot be performed. Applicant must provide a registered surveyor's field survey documenting pole locations, conductor elevations, and confirmed mid-span clearance distances for all driveway and parking areas passing beneath or adjacent to overhead electric facilities.
applicableAreas: Driveways, parking areas, and buildings within potential clearance distance of OHE

comment: Site plan references exterior lighting requirements (Block 1, Sheet 9) and notes that all exterior lighting must be full cut-off and fully shielded per Subchapter E 2.5. However, no photometric plan or lighting fixture location plan is provided showing specific decorative fixture locations in relation to the overhead electric lines documented on the site. If decorative lighting is proposed beneath or in proximity to overhead lines, clearance dimensions (7.5-foot sky-to-ground, 15-foot radial) must be provided. Applicant should clarify whether decorative lighting fixtures are proposed beneath overhead facilities and if so, provide photometric plan with clearance dimension callouts or relocation confirmation.
applicableAreas: Site lighting fixtures near overhead electric lines

comment: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows mitigation trees ('M' designation) and other plantings near the overhead electric line shown along the southern boundary of the site. Tree list (Sheet 32) provides caliper sizes and species. However, no lateral distance dimensions are shown on the landscape plan indicating how far proposed trees are located from the overhead electric conductors. Per UCM § 1.10.10.4, trees must maintain 50 lateral feet from transmission conductors (or 10 lateral feet from distribution conductors if facility is distribution rather than transmission). Tree species must be verified against ECM Appendix F 'UC' (Utility Compatible) designation for trees within the clearance zones. Applicant must provide: (1) dimension callouts showing lateral distances from OHE to all trees within 50 feet of the line; (2) confirmation that tree species are from the UC list; (3) site grading contours showing clearance compliance.
applicableAreas: Trees near overhead electric transmission lines

comment: Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4) shows utility poles and other infrastructure in the surrounding area. Site plan shows buildings positioned on the development site. However, without a clear depiction of existing streetlight pole locations adjacent to the property, the relationship between proposed buildings and streetlights cannot be verified. Applicant should confirm the locations of any existing streetlight poles in the Valley View Road ROW adjacent to the property and provide dimension callouts on the site plan showing that proposed buildings maintain adequate clearance from these existing streetlights.
applicableAreas: Buildings adjacent to existing streetlight poles

comment: Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4) shows utility poles located on the property and in adjacent ROW. While electric transmission notes on Sheet 3 reference down guy anchors as infrastructure requiring clearance coordination, the specific locations of down guy wires (support cables from distribution poles to ground anchors) are not clearly marked or detailed on the site plan. Proposed accessible paths, driveways, and site features are shown on the site plan, but without detailed down guy wire documentation, conflicts cannot be definitively verified or confirmed as resolved. If down guy wires from existing poles conflict with proposed accessible routes or driveways, applicant must provide revised utility plan showing either pole relocation or conversion to self-supporting poles, with supporting documentation.
applicableAreas: Accessible paths and driveways near existing electric poles

comment: Existing Conditions Survey (Sheet 4) shows utility poles on site and in adjacent ROW. If down guy anchors exist associated with these poles, they are not explicitly labeled or located on the survey. Easement plat (Sheet 2) does not clearly delineate dedicated down guy anchor easements showing the required 10-foot width and 5-foot extension past anchor ground entry. Applicant must provide detailed survey and easement exhibit showing down guy anchor locations (if any exist) with dedicated easements meeting the 10-foot width by 5-foot-extension specification per Austin Energy Transmission Engineering Standards.
applicableAreas: Down guy anchor locations from distribution poles

comment: Sheet 3 documents extensive construction coordination requirements for work near transmission facilities, referencing OSHA clearance requirements. However, no construction staging area plan, equipment laydown zone diagram, or work platform logistics plan is provided with the site plan submittal. During construction, equipment and materials must maintain 10-foot radial clearance from energized overhead lines per OSHA 1910.333 and UCM § 1.10.2 (this is distinct from permanent clearance requirements). Applicant must provide a detailed construction logistics plan showing staging areas, equipment operation zones, crane swing radius, and scaffold/platform locations with dimension callouts verifying 10-foot radial clearance from all overhead electric facilities during construction phases.
applicableAreas: Construction staging areas, equipment zones, and work platforms

comment: Trees are shown at 5-15 feet from OHE distribution line on the landscape plan, which falls within the 15-foot restricted zone for non-utility-compatible trees per UCM § 1.10.10.4. However, the landscape plan identifies these trees only by functional category (M, SY, PL) without specifying species. Species are identified on Sheet 35 (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud, Texas Mountain Laurel), but no verification is provided of their utility-compatible (UC) status per ECM Appendix F, which is the definitive reference for this requirement. Cannot verify compliance without documented UC status for each proposed species.
applicableAreas: southern property boundary near OHE line
parking lot edge areas near utility corridor

comment: Trees are proposed at 5-25 feet from OHE distribution line, which overlaps the 25-foot zone where large trees (40+ feet mature height per ECM Appendix F) are restricted. Plant schedule lists Cedar Elm and Live Oak as shade trees in large containers (100 gal.), which could indicate mature size potential. However, no explicit mature height documentation is provided for these species per ECM Appendix F. Cannot verify whether proposed trees will exceed the 40-foot mature height threshold that triggers this requirement.
applicableAreas: southern property boundary near OHE line
parking lot landscape areas

comment: Overhead electric poles are clearly present (indicated by '-OHE-' line on site and landscape plans, and by utility easement boundaries). However, specific pole locations are not dimensioned on either the site plan or landscape plan. Trees are shown near the OHE line but without dimensioned distances to specific pole locations. The 10-foot pole clearance requirement cannot be verified because pole positions are not precisely located relative to tree planting locations on the submitted plans.
applicableAreas: OHE line along southern boundary

comment: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows pad-mounted transformer locations. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows tree locations. However, these sheets are not dimensionally cross-referenced, and no analysis is provided showing the distance from each pad-mount transformer to nearby trees. The 10-foot clearance from pad-mount equipment centerline cannot be verified without dimensional analysis relating the two sheets.
applicableAreas: parking lot and building perimeter areas

comment: Underground electric equipment (pull boxes, utility lines) are indicated on the site plan and electrical design plan. Tree locations are shown on the landscape plan. However, no dimensional analysis or cross-reference is provided relating underground equipment locations to specific tree planting locations. The 5-foot clearance from underground equipment cannot be verified without dimensional documentation showing the relationship between proposed trees and underground utility vault/equipment locations.
applicableAreas: site-wide near utility infrastructure

comment: Root barrier requirements apply only if trees are proposed within 20 feet of underground equipment (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment). The landscape plan does not provide dimensional analysis of tree locations relative to underground equipment, so applicability cannot be determined. Additionally, no root barrier details or specifications are provided on the landscape plan or landscape details sheets. Cannot verify whether this requirement applies or, if it does, whether it is satisfied.
applicableAreas: site areas with trees near underground utilities

comment: The landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows tree symbols labeled only by functional category ('M' for mitigation tree, 'SY' for street yard tree, 'PL' for parking lot tree, 'P' for parking buffer point tree). These abbreviations indicate regulatory category, not species identification. Tree species (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud, Texas Mountain Laurel) are identified only on a separate landscape calculations sheet (Sheet 35), not on the landscape plan itself. A user reading the landscape plan cannot identify which specific tree species is shown at each location without cross-referencing to another sheet. The plant legend on the landscape plan does not include species identification.
applicableAreas: entire landscape plan, particularly trees near utility facilities

comment: Large trees (mature height 40+ feet per ECM Appendix F) require differentiation from smaller trees to verify compliance with 25-foot clearance restrictions near distribution facilities. Sheet 35 plant schedule indicates container sizes (100 gal. for shade trees, 45 gal. for ornamental trees) but does not explicitly reference mature heights per ECM Appendix F. The landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not differentiate large trees from smaller trees with any notation or symbol. While species are identifiable from Sheet 35 (Cedar Elm, Live Oak potentially 40+ feet), the plan does not explicitly mark or call out which trees are large trees for verification purposes.
applicableAreas: areas near OHE with proposed large trees

comment: The landscape plan proposes trees (mitigation trees and other categories) at approximately 5-15 feet from the overhead electric distribution line along the southern property boundary, which falls within the utility easement area (5-foot electric easement per site plan) and within the 15-foot restricted clearance zone per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Site plan notes reference a '5' Electric Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14' and '5' Elec. & Tele. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 885'. Proposed trees are located within or immediately adjacent to this utility easement without documented written approval from Austin Energy. No approval letter, permit exception, or authorization from Austin Energy is provided in the submitted plan set for any trees in utility easement areas. Variations to planting distances within utility easements require explicit written approval per UCM § 1.10.10.4.
applicableAreas: southern property boundary within 5-foot electric utility easement
areas within 15 feet of OHE distribution line

comment: Transformer pads appear to be located 3-5 feet from adjacent building footprints, which is less than the minimum 5-foot clearance required. No dimension annotations on the electrical plan document compliance with this clearance standard.
applicableAreas: All 5 transformer pad locations; west side pads near Buildings 1, 2, 8; east side pad near Building 4; central pad near Buildings 6-7

comment: Transformer pad hot-stick access areas appear to lack minimum 10-foot clearance to adjacent building structures. No access door orientation is identified, and no clearance dimensions are provided to verify compliance.
applicableAreas: All 5 transformer pads; buildings 1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 8

comment: Transformer pads appear to be located within or immediately adjacent to Public Utility Easement (PUE) corridors marked on the plan. Placement of electrical equipment within utility easements requires written Austin Energy Design approval, which is not documented in the submittal.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads 1 and 2 (west side, near Buildings 1 and 2); potentially pad 3 (east side)

comment: Transformer pads are located within Public Utility Easement (PUE) and other utility easement corridors without documented Austin Energy Design written approval for such placement. Applicant must provide AE Design approval letter or revise pad locations to avoid easement conflicts.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads 1, 2, 3 located within utility easement corridors

comment: Transformer easements are not shown on any sheet of the site plan. Austin Energy requires transformer easements to be depicted and dimensioned around all pads for accessibility and maintenance. Applicant must add transformer easement exhibits showing required width (to be confirmed by AE Design).
applicableAreas: All 5 transformer pad locations

comment: Transformer pad construction details and specifications matching Austin Energy Design-approved standards are not provided. Applicant must obtain transformer pad detail sheets from AE Design and add them to construction details, showing dimensions and specifications for the proposed single-phase or three-phase service type.
applicableAreas: All 5 transformer pad locations

comment: All transformer pads are positioned within 4 feet of vehicle circulation routes and therefore require protective bollards. No bollards are shown on the electrical plan or detailed in construction details. Applicant must add 4-inch diameter galvanized rigid metal bollard details to the construction detail sheets and indicate bollard locations on Sheet 21, spaced to allow equipment door opening per AE Design equipment pad specifications.
applicableAreas: All 5 transformer pads; locations: west side pads near Buildings 1, 2, 8; east side pad near Building 4; central pad near Buildings 6-7

comment: Retaining walls are present on the site. However, no clearance dimensions are labeled showing the distance from transformer pads to retaining walls. Applicant must add dimension annotations confirming minimum 5-foot clearance from transformer pad edges to all retaining walls.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad locations and adjacent retaining walls (multiple locations)

comment: Fencing is present on the site. No access door orientation is identified for transformer pads, and no clearance dimensions are shown from transformer pads to fence lines. Applicant must add dimension annotations identifying access door orientation and confirming appropriate clearances (5 feet for operator sides, 3 feet for non-operator sides) from removable ventilated fences.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads with adjacent fencing

comment: If transformer pads are proposed with clearances less than 5 feet to buildings, applicant must provide: (1) written Austin Energy Design approval, (2) architectural specifications confirming 3-hour fire rating in clearance areas, (3) verification that location does not face confined space, (4) confirmation of 10+ feet clearance to windows/doors/ducts, and (5) verification of 15+ feet vertical clearance to windows/doors/ducts.
applicableAreas: West side transformer pads if reduced clearances to buildings are proposed

comment: Building elevation drawings are not provided. Without elevations showing balcony and overhang locations, clearances from transformer pads to these features cannot be verified. Applicant must provide building elevation drawings with dimension callouts confirming minimum 5-foot lateral clearance from transformer pads to all balconies and overhangs, or confirm that overhead structures are not directly above pads.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads in proximity to building balconies and overhangs

comment: Building elevation drawings and window/door/vent locations are not provided. Transformer type (oil-filled vs. dry-type) is not specified. Applicant must provide: (1) specification of transformer equipment type, (2) building elevations identifying all windows, doors, and ventilating ducts, and (3) dimension callouts confirming 12-foot minimum horizontal clearance from oil-filled equipment edges to any low windows/doors/ducts.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads if oil-filled equipment with adjacent windows, doors, or vents

comment: Sidewalks are present on the site. No dimension annotations confirm minimum 2-foot clearance from transformer pad edges to back of sidewalks. Applicant must add dimension callouts showing 2-foot minimum distance maintained from all transformer pads to adjacent sidewalk back edges.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads adjacent to sidewalks

comment: Building floor plans showing fire exit stairwell locations are not provided in the site plan submittal. Applicant must provide building floor plans identifying exit stair locations and dimension callouts confirming adequate clearance from transformer pads to all fire exit stairs.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads in proximity to building fire exit stairwells

comment: Building elevation drawings are not provided. Transformer type (oil-filled vs. dry-type) is not specified. Applicant must provide building elevations identifying fire escape locations (if any) and confirm 20-foot minimum horizontal/radial clearance from oil-filled transformer pad edges to fire escapes or exterior stairs serving as fire escapes.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads if oil-filled equipment and fire escapes present

comment: A fire hydrant is shown on the site plan. No dimension annotations confirm minimum 5-foot clearance from transformer pads to the fire hydrant. Applicant must add clearance dimension callout(s) verifying 5-foot minimum distance maintained from all transformer pads to the fire hydrant.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads relative to the site's fire hydrant

comment: Landscape plan shows trees and shrubs throughout the site. No documentation confirms that tree species are identified as utility-compatible per ECM Appendix F. Applicant must cross-reference the tree list (Sheet 32) against ECM Appendix F 'UC' column and confirm all trees within 10 feet of transformer pads and 15 feet of overhead conductors are utility-compatible species, or revise landscape plan.
applicableAreas: Trees shown on landscape plan (Sheet 31) within 10 feet of transformer pads and 15 feet of overhead conductors

comment: Landscape plan shows shrubs and groundcover throughout the site. No access door orientation is marked on transformer pads, and no clearance dimensions are provided. Applicant must identify access door orientation for each transformer pad and provide dimension callouts confirming 10-foot minimum lateral clearance from access door side and 5-foot minimum from other sides to all adjacent shrubs/vegetation.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads with adjacent shrubs and low-lying vegetation

comment: Landscape plan shows trees within 20 feet of transformer pad locations. No root barrier details or specifications are provided. Applicant must add root barrier detail sheets showing 4-foot minimum depth and 5-foot distance from transformer equipment for all trees within 20 lateral feet of pads, and add root barrier callouts to landscape plan.
applicableAreas: Trees shown on landscape plan within 20 lateral feet of transformer pads

comment: Trash collection area is shown on site plan. No dimension annotations confirm minimum 5-foot clearance from transformer pads to dumpster(s). Applicant must add clearance dimension callouts verifying 5-foot minimum distance from all transformer pads to waste containers/dumpsters.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads relative to trash collection/dumpster area

comment: Bicycle parking is provided on site. No dimension annotations confirm minimum 5-foot clearance from transformer pads to bicycle racks. Applicant must add clearance dimension callouts verifying 5-foot minimum distance from all transformer pads to bike racks.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads relative to bicycle parking locations

comment: Light poles are present on the site plan. No dimension annotations confirm minimum 5-foot clearance from transformer pads to light poles. Applicant must add clearance dimension callouts verifying 5-foot minimum distance from all transformer pads to lighting poles.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads relative to lighting poles

comment: Fire lanes are designated on the fire protection plan. No dimension annotations confirm minimum 15-foot clearance from transformer pads to fire lane boundaries. Applicant must add clearance dimension callouts verifying 15-foot minimum distance from all transformer pads to fire lanes.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads relative to designated fire lanes

comment: Five transformer pads are proposed on the site. No dimension callouts confirm minimum 5-foot clearance between individual transformer pads. Applicant must add clearance dimension annotations between all transformer pads verifying compliance with 5-foot minimum spacing requirement.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations relative to each other

comment: Water lines are shown on utility plan. No dimension annotations confirm minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from transformer pads to water lines. Applicant must add clearance dimension callouts or provide utility coordination drawings verifying 5-foot minimum distance from all transformer pads to water service lines.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads relative to water service lines

comment: Wastewater lines are shown on utility plan. No dimension annotations confirm minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from transformer pads to wastewater lines. Applicant must add clearance dimension callouts or provide utility coordination drawings verifying 5-foot minimum distance from all transformer pads to wastewater service lines.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads relative to wastewater service lines

comment: Storm drain lines are shown on site plans. No dimension annotations confirm minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from transformer pads to storm drain lines. Applicant must add clearance dimension callouts or provide utility coordination drawings verifying 5-foot minimum distance from all transformer pads to storm drain infrastructure.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads relative to storm drain lines

comment: Underground utility lines are shown at various locations. No utility coordination drawings, profiles, or cross-sections show vertical and horizontal clearances from transformer pads to other underground utilities. Applicant must provide utility coordination drawings with dimension callouts confirming 12-inch minimum horizontal and vertical clearance (OD to OD) from transformer pads to all other underground utilities.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations relative to underground utilities

comment: Electrical plan shows transformer pads and underground utilities at the same location. No profile or cross-section drawings show vertical relationships between transformer facilities and other utilities. Applicant must provide utility coordination profile drawings confirming transformer pads and underground electrical facilities are not located directly over or under other utility lines.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations with coexisting underground utilities

comment: Overhead distribution lines are shown on utility plan. No dimension annotations or profile drawings confirm 7.5-foot minimum horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from transformer pad locations to overhead distribution conductors. Applicant must add profile cross-sections or dimension callouts verifying 7.5-foot clearance from ground level vertically through conductor height.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads under or near overhead distribution conductors

comment: Overhead distribution lines are shown on utility plan. No dimension annotations confirm 15-foot radius clearance from transformer pads to overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors (measured from conductors, not pole centerline). Applicant must add clearance dimension callouts or overlay 15-foot radius circles around overhead conductors demonstrating compliance.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads relative to overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors

comment: Site plan shows integrated garage parking. No cross-section drawings are provided showing vertical clearances at transformer pad locations to verify adequate headroom and overhead clearance for equipment access and operation.
applicableAreas: Transformer pads with overhead structures or parking garage proximity

comment: Transformer equipment type (oil-filled vs. dry-type) is not specified. If oil-filled equipment is proposed, applicant must provide grading plan with drainage arrows showing surface water slope direction around transformer pads, confirming liquid/drainage flow is directed away from buildings.
applicableAreas: Oil-filled transformer pads (if proposed) and surrounding grading

comment: Electrical routing from transformer pads to meters is shown but not dimensioned relative to property lines. Applicant must provide annotated routing with dimension callouts confirming all electrical conduit from transformer pads to meters remains 100% on private property and does not cross into public right-of-way or restricted easements.
applicableAreas: Electrical routing from transformer pads to meters

comment: Overhead distribution facilities are shown on utility plan. No profile or cross-section drawings verify that customer buildings, parking structures, and other facilities do not extend vertically into overhead conductor space. Applicant must provide utility coordination profile drawings confirming no customer facilities are located directly under overhead distribution lines.
applicableAreas: Customer buildings and structures relative to overhead distribution lines
